title: Microsoft Viva: Cowork adoption and impact in the Consumption Dashboard and Copilot Dashboard
summary: Hold: the consumption query is described as returning daily data without mentioning that it defaults to weekly grouping. The page also sends administrators to a feature-access page that does not supply the identification feature ID it promises; the documented identification and manager-setting paths and the roadmap facts otherwise check out.

## October 06, 2026
What changed: The Consumption dashboard and Copilot dashboard now include expanded metrics on Cowork adoption and its impact. Analysts can export data and use the new Consumption query in advanced insights to explore all metrics.

claims.where: What's changing: consumption query output granularity
claims.claim: Following the printed consumption-query route returns the metrics per person, service and day.
claims.quote: Source data is PersonId, ServiceId, and MetricDate (one row per person, per service, per day). By default, consumption queries are grouped by week. To change this to day or month, select More Settings under the Description box.
claims.fix: Replace 'which returns four preselected credit metrics per person, service and day, with no other metric categories added' with 'which has four preselected consumption metrics and cannot add other metric categories. Its source data is per person, service and day, but queries are grouped by week by default; for daily grouping, select More Settings under the Description box and set Group by to Day.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/insights/advanced/analyst/ai-cost-query.

claims.claim: Other metric categories cannot be added to the consumption query.
claims.quote: You can't add other metric categories. To remove a metric, select the "X" on it.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; summary
claims.claim: A dedicated VFAM policy governs who can identify users and view identified outputs.
claims.quote: Access is governed by a dedicated Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM) policy, so administrators decide exactly who in the organization can identify users and view identified outputs.

claims.claim: Identification policies apply to Consumption Dashboard insights and data export.
claims.quote: Identification is available for the following Viva Insights features: Consumption Dashboard data export and Consumption Dashboard insights

claims.claim: Only a Microsoft 365 Global Administrator or AI Administrator can create and manage identification policies, using either UI or PowerShell.
claims.quote: Only a Microsoft 365 Global Administrator or an AI Administrator can create and manage identification access policies. Either role can perform every step, in both the Microsoft 365 admin center and PowerShell.

claims.claim: Identification is reached in the Microsoft 365 admin center through Settings > Org settings > Viva feature access > Viva Insights > identification feature.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Org settings > Viva feature access, select Viva Insights, choose the identification feature, and add a policy.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId <FeatureId> -Name <PolicyName> -IsFeatureEnabled $true creates an enabling feature-access policy using Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy
-FeatureId <String>
-IsFeatureEnabled <Boolean>
-ModuleId <String>
-Name <String>
The IsFeatureEnabled parameter specifies whether or not the feature is enabled by the policy. Valid values are: $true: The feature is enabled by the policy.

claims.claim: Identification policies can be scoped to users, groups or the tenant.
claims.quote:
Group or user level | Pilots, phased rollouts, and specific cohorts. Targets Microsoft Entra groups or individual users.
Tenant level | A global default applied to everyone in the organization.

claims.claim: A group or user identification policy allows up to 20 users or groups in total.
claims.quote: Up to 20 users/groups per policy; up to 10 policies per feature.

claims.claim: There can be one tenant-wide identification policy per feature.
claims.quote: Tenant level | A global default applied to everyone in the organization. | One tenant-wide policy per feature.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown despite the published licensing for the surrounding Viva Insights product.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot plans also include manager, leader, and advanced analysis for all employees who have an assigned Copilot license.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Add to licensing.notes and the Licence paragraph: 'The general Viva Insights requirement is applicable Viva Insights licensing and a Microsoft 365 or Office 365 tenant with Exchange Online Plan 1 or Plan 2. Microsoft Copilot plans include manager, leader, and advanced analysis for employees assigned a Copilot license; a license specific to the Cowork views is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/insights/advanced/setup-maint/environment-requirements. Searches for Consumption Dashboard license Cowork and Consumption Dashboard pricing/licensing found no Cowork-view-specific entitlement; this is the standard's minor product-level licensing understatement, not evidence of a new reporting charge.

claims.claim: The reporting change adds no documented change to Cowork's action capabilities.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Insights Consumption Dashboard reporting does not change Cowork access capabilities; read dashboard, query and export pages. Their documented operations monitor consumption or extract data; no change to Cowork action capabilities is described.
